sn42.11:1.1: Uruvelakappa of the Mallas is mentioned a few times in the Suttas ([sn48.52:1.2](), [an9.41:1.1]()). Elsewhere I can only find an Urubilvākalpa in the Lalitavistara (Vaidya 297), which however is apparently simply the well-known Uruvelā near where the Buddha was awakened.
sn42.11:1.3: While this might seem like a generic question, the phrase “origin and disappearance of suffering” appears elsewhere only in the context of dependent origination ([sn12.43:1.2](), [sn35.106:1.1]()). It is unusual to see an obscure lay person directly asking on this topic. The Buddha’s response shows that he did not think Bhadraka would understand the standard explanation, in terms of the arising of sense activity leading to continuation of rebirth. But rather than dismissing the problem as too hard, he takes an approach that Bhadraka can relate to.
sn42.11:1.5: Dependent origination is realized at the time of stream-entry, when a person finally overcomes all doubt, including doubts such as “Did I exist in the past?” or “Will I exist on the future?”
sn42.11:2.2: Notice that, while the Buddha is focusing on the present, he does not mean narrowly, “the present moment arisen in awareness”. It is a broader sense of present requiring reflection and inference regarding hypotheticals.
